words.definition: to judge how good, useful or successful something is

meet.sentence: At the end of the year, the teachers {evaluate} every student's project.

questions.prompt: to judge how good, useful or successful something is

questions.sentence: Before choosing a university, it's smart to {_} all your options carefully.
The judges will {evaluate} each song and choose a winner.
questions.explain: Correct. Judges evaluate: they decide how good something is.

questions.sentence: I {evaluated} my sandwich because I was really hungry.
questions.explain: Evaluate means to judge how good something is. When you're hungry, you eat your sandwich.

questions.them: Did the teacher like your presentation? 😬
questions.me: She'll {_} it tomorrow and give us feedback.

questions.them: Why do you read so many reviews before buying a phone?
questions.me: I want to {_} every option before I spend 3,000 shekels!

questions.sentence: The teacher's {_} of my essay was very fair.
questions.hint: You need a noun after 'the teacher's'. Many nouns end in -ion.

questions.sentence: The new program will be {_} after six months to see if it really works.
questions.explain: 'To see if it really works' means judging it: evaluated.

words.definition: to make certain that something happens or is true

meet.sentence: Please check the address twice to {ensure} the letter arrives on time.

questions.prompt: to make certain that something happens or is true

questions.sentence: Wear a helmet to {_} that you stay safe on your bike.
The school hired more guards to {ensure} that students are safe.
questions.explain: Correct. Ensure = make certain that something happens.

questions.sentence: My grandmother {ensured} me a cup of tea when I visited.
questions.explain: Ensure means to make certain. Your grandmother made or gave you tea.

questions.them: Are you sure we'll get tickets for the concert? 🎤
questions.me: Yes! I'll buy them online tonight to {_} we get good seats.

questions.them: Why do you always set three alarms? 😂
questions.me: To {_} I'm never late for the bus again!

options.text: The coach {ensured} that every player had water.
She {ensured} her keys in her bag.
I {ensured} a new pair of shoes at the mall.

questions.explain: You ensure that something happens (make certain). You put keys in a bag and buy shoes.

words.definition: to make something smaller in size, amount or number

meet.sentence: The city wants to {reduce} traffic by building more bike lanes.

questions.prompt: to make something smaller in size, amount or number

questions.sentence: Turning off the lights when you leave a room can {_} your electricity bill.
Drinking less soda can {reduce} the risk of health problems.
questions.explain: Correct. You can reduce a risk, a price, an amount or a number.

questions.sentence: He {reduced} the stairs to the third floor.
questions.explain: Reduce means to make something smaller or less. On stairs, you climb or go up.

questions.them: You're on your phone way less lately. How?
questions.me: I turned off notifications to {_} how much I use it 📵

questions.them: Did the store really lower the prices for Black Friday?
questions.me: Yes! They {_} everything by 30%. I got new headphones 🎧

questions.sentence: There was a big {_} in the number of car accidents after the new law.
questions.hint: You need a noun after 'a big'. Many nouns end in -tion.

questions.sentence: The fire {_} the old building to ashes in just one hour.
questions.explain: Reduce something to ashes (or pieces) = destroy it until only that is left.

words.definition: to show what something is like; also, to think carefully about something

meet.sentence: Her excellent grades {reflect} how hard she worked this year.

questions.prompt: to show what something is like, or to be a sign of it
to think carefully and seriously about something

questions.sentence: The colorful paintings on the walls {_} the happy mood of the school.
After the trip, the teacher asked us to {_} on what we had learned.
The lake {reflected} the mountains like a mirror.
questions.explain: Correct. Water and mirrors reflect images: they show them back.

questions.sentence: I {reflected} my bike to school this morning.
questions.explain: Reflect means to show something or think about it. You ride a bike.

questions.them: You've been so quiet since the trip. Everything OK?
questions.me: Yeah, I just need some time to {_} on everything that happened.

questions.them: Why does everyone love this song so much?
questions.me: The words really {_} how teenagers feel 💯

questions.sentence: Writing in a diary every night gives you time for {_}.
questions.hint: You need a noun after 'time for'. Many nouns end in -ion.

options.text: She looked at her {reflection} in the shop window.
Take a moment to {reflect} before you answer.
He {reflected} the ball to his teammate.

questions.explain: Reflect can mean show (clothes reflect your personality) or think (reflect before you answer), and a reflection is the image in a mirror or window. You pass a ball.

words.definition: large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed

meet.sentence: Moving to a new country was a {significant} change in my life.

questions.prompt: large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed

questions.sentence: Winning the national competition was the most {_} moment in the school's history.
Social media has had a {significant} effect on how teenagers communicate.
questions.explain: Correct. A significant effect is a big, important one.

questions.sentence: I'm feeling {significant} today, so I'm staying in bed.
questions.explain: Significant describes something large or important, not how you feel. You might be feeling sick or tired.

questions.them: Was the price difference between the two phones big?
questions.me: Yeah, it was {_}: almost 1,000 shekels!

questions.them: Why is today such a big deal for your grandparents? 🎉
questions.me: It's their 50th anniversary! A really {_} day for our family.

questions.sentence: Prices have gone up {_} since last year: almost everything costs more.
questions.hint: You need an adverb that describes 'gone up'. Many adverbs end in -ly.

questions.sentence: Few people understood the {_} of the discovery at the time.
questions.explain: After 'the' you need a noun: significance = importance.

words.definition: completely necessary; you cannot do without it

meet.sentence: Water is {essential} for all living things.

questions.prompt: completely necessary; you cannot do without it

questions.sentence: A good pair of shoes is {_} if you're going to hike for six hours.
Sleep is {essential} for your memory and concentration.
questions.explain: Correct. Essential = completely necessary.

questions.sentence: The movie was so {essential} that I fell asleep.
questions.explain: Essential means necessary. A movie that makes you fall asleep is boring.

questions.them: What should I pack for the trip to the desert? 🏜️
questions.me: Water is {_}! Take at least three bottles.

questions.them: Do I really need to go to the review class before the exam?
questions.me: Trust me, it's {_}. The teacher explains everything that will be on the test.

questions.sentence: The two phones are {_} the same: only the color is different.
questions.hint: You need an adverb before 'the same'. Many adverbs end in -ly.

questions.sentence: Before the trip, pack only the {_}: water, a hat and sunscreen.
questions.explain: Here you need a plural noun: the essentials = the most necessary things.

words.definition: correct and true in every detail

meet.sentence: The weather app is usually {accurate}: when it says rain, it rains.

questions.prompt: correct and true in every detail

questions.sentence: Make sure your answers are {_}: check every number twice.
The witness gave the police an {accurate} description of the thief.
questions.explain: Correct. An accurate description is correct in every detail.

questions.sentence: My little brother is very {accurate}: he's always laughing.
questions.explain: Accurate means correct in every detail. Someone who's always laughing is cheerful or funny.

questions.them: Is it true that the trip is on Thursday? Someone said Friday 🤔
questions.me: Ask the teacher. What people say in the group chat isn't always {_}.

questions.them: How do you know exactly how many steps you walked today?
questions.me: My watch counts them. It's very {_}!

questions.sentence: Doctors need to measure your blood pressure {_}.
questions.hint: You need an adverb that describes 'measure'. Many adverbs end in -ly.

questions.sentence: The new cameras improve the {_} of the speed checks on the highway.
questions.explain: After 'the' you need a noun: accuracy.

words.definition: lasting for only a short time; not permanent

meet.sentence: While our school was being fixed, we studied in a {temporary} building.

questions.prompt: lasting for only a short time; not permanent

questions.sentence: My cousin got a {_} job at a café, just for the summer holidays.
The pain after the injection is only {temporary}.
questions.explain: Correct. Temporary = it lasts only a short time.

questions.sentence: We ate a {temporary} pizza with extra cheese.
questions.explain: Temporary describes things that last a short time, like a job or a building. For a pizza, you'd say delicious.

questions.them: Is the road to Eilat closed forever?? 😱
questions.me: No, don't worry, it's {_}. They're fixing it until Sunday.

questions.them: You changed your hair color?? I love it!
questions.me: Thanks! It's only {_}: it washes out after a week 💜

questions.sentence: The swimming pool is {_} closed for cleaning.
questions.hint: You need an adverb before 'closed'. Change the -y to -i and add -ly.

options.text: {Temporary} workers are hired for the busy season.
Feeling sad after a breakup is usually {temporary}.
The school built a {temporary} classroom in the yard.
My dog is very {temporary} and loves to play.

questions.explain: Temporary is for things that last a short time and then end: a job, a feeling, a building. A dog that loves to play is playful.

words.definition: a result of something that happened, often a bad one

meet.sentence: If you don't study, you'll have to live with the {consequences}.

questions.prompt: a result of something that happened, often a bad one

questions.sentence: One {_} of the storm was that the whole town lost electricity.
Missing the bus had a serious {consequence}: I was late for the exam.
questions.explain: Correct. A consequence is a result, often a bad one.

questions.sentence: Happy birthday! Here's a small {consequence} for you.
questions.explain: A consequence is a result of something. On a birthday, you give someone a present or a gift.

questions.them: Why do you look so tired? 😴
questions.me: I played video games until 2am. Now I'm living with the {_} 😩

questions.them: Is it a big deal if I ignore the lab safety rules?
questions.me: Yes! It can have serious {_}. Someone got burned last year.

questions.sentence: He didn't train all winter and, {_}, he lost the race.
questions.hint: You need an adverb that means 'as a result'. Many adverbs end in -ly.

questions.sentence: Which bus you take is of no {_}: they both stop near the school.
questions.explain: 'Of no consequence' is a formal way to say 'not important'.

meet.sentence: The exchange program gave me the {opportunity} to live in London for a month.

questions.sentence: Don't miss this {_} to meet the famous author: she visits only once a year.
The summer job was a great {opportunity} to save money.
questions.explain: Correct. An opportunity is a chance to do something.

questions.sentence: I fell off my bike and got a big {opportunity} on my knee.
questions.explain: An opportunity is a chance. On your knee, you'd get a bruise or a cut.

questions.them: They're looking for volunteers at the animal shelter 🐾
questions.me: Really? That's a great {_} to help and get experience!

questions.them: Should I try out for the national team? I'm scared 😬
questions.me: Go for it! You might not get another {_} like this.

questions.sentence: Equal {_} for men and women at work are still not guaranteed in many countries.
questions.explain: 'Equal opportunities' means everyone gets the same chances.

words.definition: facts or signs that show that something is true

meet.sentence: The police found {evidence} that the thief came in through the window.

questions.prompt: facts or signs that show that something is true

questions.sentence: There is no scientific {_} that eating carrots helps you see in the dark.
The muddy shoes by the door were {evidence} that someone had been outside.
questions.explain: Correct. Evidence is something that shows that something is true.

questions.sentence: I'd like an {evidence} with cheese and tomato, please.
questions.explain: Evidence is proof that something is true. In a café you'd order a sandwich or a toast.

questions.them: Did Dana really eat the whole cake? 🎂
questions.me: She says no, but there's chocolate all over her face. That's pretty clear {_}! 😂

questions.them: My brother says he did his homework, but I don't believe him.
questions.me: Ask him for {_}. Tell him to show you his notebook!

questions.sentence: It was {_} from her smile that she had passed the test.
questions.hint: You need an adjective after 'It was'. Take off the -ce and add -t.

questions.sentence: The lawyer showed the court three new pieces of {_}.
questions.explain: Evidence is uncountable: say 'pieces of evidence', never 'evidences'.

words.definition: a strong effect that something has on someone or something

meet.sentence: The new phone ban had a big {impact} on how students spend their breaks.

questions.prompt: a strong effect that something has on someone or something

questions.sentence: Your teachers can have a huge {_} on the way you see the world.
Climate change has a serious {impact} on farmers in hot countries.
questions.explain: Correct. Something has an impact on someone or something.

questions.sentence: Can you pass me the {impact}? I want to cut the bread.
questions.explain: An impact is a strong effect. To cut bread, you need a knife.

questions.them: Did that video about plastic really change how you shop? 🤔
questions.me: Totally! It had a big {_} on me. I don't buy bottled water anymore.

questions.them: Why did you choose to become a nurse?
questions.me: My aunt is a nurse. She had a huge {_} on my decision ❤️

questions.sentence: Rising prices will {_} families with small children the most.
questions.explain: Impact can also be a verb: to impact something = to have a strong effect on it.
